```{r, include = FALSE}
has_sf <- requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = has_sf,
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 2.4,
  dev.args = list(bg = "white")
)
```

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(a5R)
library(sf)
```

```{r helpers, include = FALSE}
# Plotting helpers for the figures; the a5R calls are in the visible chunks.
pal <- list(
  a = "#2a78d6", b = "#eb6834", result = "#1baf7a",
  base = "#e4e3df", ink = "#333333", muted = "#8a8984"
)
ramp <- c("#cde2fb", "#9ec5f4", "#6da7ec", "#3987e5", "#256abf", "#184f95", "#0d366b")

cells_of <- function(x) a5_cell_to_boundary(if (is_a5_covering(x)) a5_uncompact(x) else x)

# The cells a covering stores, decoded from its bytes (marker dropped).
stored_cells <- function(x) {
  b <- unclass(x)[[1]]
  n <- length(b) %/% 8
  hex <- vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    paste(rev(as.character(b[(8 * i - 7):(8 * i)])), collapse = "")
  }, "")
  a5_cell(hex[-n])
}

panels <- function(n, top = 1.6) {
  par(mfrow = c(1, n), mar = c(0.2, 0.2, top, 0.2), xpd = NA)
}

frame <- function(..., main = "", pad = 0.04) {
  bbs <- lapply(list(...), function(g) unclass(wk::wk_bbox(g)))
  xr <- range(unlist(lapply(bbs, `[`, c("xmin", "xmax"))))
  yr <- range(unlist(lapply(bbs, `[`, c("ymin", "ymax"))))
  xr <- xr + c(-1, 1) * pad * diff(xr)
  yr <- yr + c(-1, 1) * pad * diff(yr)
  plot.new()
  plot.window(xr, yr, asp = 1 / cos(mean(yr) * pi / 180))
  title(main, cex.main = 0.85, font.main = 1, col.main = pal$ink, line = 0.4)
}

fill <- function(g, col, border = "white", lwd = 0.4) {
  if (length(g) > 0) plot(g, col = col, border = border, lwd = lwd, add = TRUE)
}

outline <- function(g, col = pal$ink, lwd = 1.2, lty = 1) {
  plot(g, col = NA, border = col, lwd = lwd, lty = lty, add = TRUE)
}

circle <- function(cell, radius) {
  ll <- a5_cell_to_lonlat(cell, as_dataframe = TRUE)
  t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 200)
  d <- radius / 6371008.8 * 180 / pi
  wk::wkt(sprintf("LINESTRING (%s)", paste(
    ll$lon + d * cos(t) / cos(ll$lat * pi / 180), ll$lat + d * sin(t),
    collapse = ", "
  )))
}

note <- function(text) {
  mtext(text, side = 1, line = -0.6, cex = 0.7, col = pal$muted)
}
```

A *covering* is a set of A5 cells at one resolution that stands for an area:
the cells of a polygon, of a disk around a cell, or of a cap of a given
radius. An `a5_covering` vector holds one covering per element, so coverings
sit in a data frame column next to the features they describe.

## What a covering stores

A covering is stored compacted: every complete group of four sibling cells
is replaced by their parent, and a trailing *compaction marker* records the
resolution the stored cells stand for.

```{r what}
raleigh <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-78.64, 35.78, resolution = 11)
cap <- a5_spherical_cap(raleigh, radius = 12000)
cap
```

```{r what-plot, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 2.8}
stored <- stored_cells(cap)
res <- a5_get_resolution(stored)
layout(matrix(1:3, 1), widths = c(1, 1, 0.4))
par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.2), xpd = NA, cex = 1)
frame(cells_of(cap), main = sprintf("Stands for: %d cells at resolution 11", a5_count(cap)))
fill(cells_of(cap), pal$a)
frame(cells_of(cap), main = sprintf("Stores: %d cells at mixed resolutions", length(stored)))
fill(a5_cell_to_boundary(stored), paste0(ramp[c(2, 4, 6)][res - 8], "b0"), border = pal$ink)
plot.new()
legend("left", bty = "n", cex = 0.75, fill = ramp[c(6, 4, 2)], border = NA,
       legend = paste("res", 11:9), text.col = pal$ink)
```

The stored cells are parents in the A5 index, whose outlines do not nest:
drawn directly they overlap their neighbours and leave gaps. Everything that
combines, tests or measures coverings works on the stored cells without
expanding them, which keeps it fast for coverings that stand for millions of
cells. To draw a covering or join it to data keyed by cell, expand it with
`a5_uncompact()`, as every figure here does.

## Building coverings

`a5_polygon_to_cells()` returns one covering per feature. By default a cell
belongs when its centre lies inside the polygon; `containment =
"overlapping"` also takes every cell the boundary touches, so the cells
cover the polygon without gaps.

```{r polygons}
nc <- st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
nc <- st_transform(nc, 4326) # A5 works in WGS 84 longitude and latitude
alleghany <- nc[nc$NAME == "Alleghany", ]

centre <- a5_polygon_to_cells(alleghany, resolution = 11)
overlapping <- a5_polygon_to_cells(alleghany, resolution = 11, containment = "overlapping")
c(centre, overlapping)
```

```{r polygons-plot, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 2.6}
county <- wk::as_wkb(st_geometry(alleghany))
panels(2)
frame(cells_of(overlapping), main = 'containment = "centre"')
fill(cells_of(centre), pal$a)
outline(county)
frame(cells_of(overlapping), main = 'containment = "overlapping"')
fill(cells_of(overlapping), pal$a)
outline(county)
```

The functions that start from a cell return one covering per centre cell:
`a5_grid_disk()` takes every cell within `k` steps, `a5_spherical_cap()`
every cell whose centre is within a distance, and `a5_cell_to_subcell()`
the finer cells whose centres lie inside a coarser cell.

```{r around}
disk <- a5_grid_disk(raleigh, k = 3)
cap <- a5_spherical_cap(raleigh, radius = 8000)
coarse <- a5_cell_to_parent(raleigh, resolution = 9)
subcells <- a5_cell_to_subcell(coarse, resolution = 11)
```

```{r around-plot, echo = FALSE}
panels(3)
frame(cells_of(disk), main = "a5_grid_disk(k = 3)")
fill(cells_of(disk), pal$a)
fill(cells_of(raleigh), pal$ink)
frame(cells_of(cap), circle(raleigh, 8000), main = "a5_spherical_cap(8 km)")
fill(cells_of(cap), pal$a)
lines(wk::wk_coords(circle(raleigh, 8000))[, c("x", "y")], col = pal$ink, lwd = 1.2)
fill(cells_of(raleigh), pal$ink)
frame(cells_of(subcells), cells_of(coarse), main = "a5_cell_to_subcell(res 9 to 11)")
fill(cells_of(subcells), pal$a)
outline(cells_of(coarse), lwd = 1.6)
```

`a5_compact()` turns any set of cells into a covering, and
`as_a5_covering()` builds coverings from cell lists or from the stored form
written by other A5 libraries.

## Measuring coverings

`a5_count()` gives the number of cells a covering stands for, and
`a5_area()` its area. A5 cells are equal-area, so the area is the count
times the area of one cell. At resolution 11, where a cell covers about
8 km², it tracks each county's true area closely:

```{r measures}
nc$cells <- a5_polygon_to_cells(nc, resolution = 11)
nc$cell_area <- a5_area(nc$cells, units = "km^2")
head(nc[c("NAME", "cells", "cell_area")], 3)
```

```{r measures-plot, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 3.6, fig.height = 3.4, fig.align = "center"}
true_area <- as.numeric(units::set_units(st_area(nc), "km^2"))
par(mar = c(3.2, 3.6, 0.6, 0.6), mgp = c(2.1, 0.5, 0), tcl = -0.25,
    col.axis = pal$muted, col.lab = pal$ink, cex.axis = 0.75, cex.lab = 0.8)
lim <- range(0, true_area, nc$cell_area)
plot(NULL, xlim = lim, ylim = lim, asp = 1, bty = "n", las = 1,
     xlab = "County area (km²)", ylab = "Covering area (km²)")
abline(h = pretty(lim), v = pretty(lim), col = "#f0efec", lwd = 0.8)
abline(0, 1, col = pal$muted, lwd = 1, lty = 2)
points(true_area, nc$cell_area, pch = 21, bg = pal$a, col = "white", cex = 1.1)
```

Each point is a county; the dashed line marks equal areas. The covering
area is within 1% of the county's for the median county and about 6% at
worst, because each cell straddling a county boundary is in or out by its
centre. Finer resolutions reduce the error.

## Combining coverings

`a5_union()`, `a5_intersect()` and `a5_difference()` combine coverings
without expanding them.

```{r combine}
a <- a5_spherical_cap(a5_lonlat_to_cell(-78.72, 35.78, 11), radius = 10000)
b <- a5_spherical_cap(a5_lonlat_to_cell(-78.58, 35.78, 11), radius = 10000)
a5_union(a, b)
a5_intersect(a, b)
a5_difference(a, b)
```

```{r combine-plot, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 2}
both <- cells_of(a5_union(a, b))
panels(4)
frame(both, main = "a and b")
fill(cells_of(a), paste0(pal$a, "b0"))
fill(cells_of(b), paste0(pal$b, "b0"))
centres <- a5_cell_to_lonlat(a5_lonlat_to_cell(c(-78.79, -78.51), 35.78, 11), as_dataframe = TRUE)
text(centres$lon, centres$lat, c("a", "b"), col = "white", font = 2, cex = 1.2)
for (step in list(list(a5_union(a, b), "a5_union(a, b)"),
                  list(a5_intersect(a, b), "a5_intersect(a, b)"),
                  list(a5_difference(a, b), "a5_difference(a, b)"))) {
  frame(both, main = step[[2]])
  fill(both, pal$base)
  fill(cells_of(step[[1]]), pal$result)
}
```

They work element by element, recycling a length-one argument, so one call
intersects every county with a single cap. With one argument, `a5_union()`
merges every covering in a vector into one.

```{r recycle}
near_raleigh <- a5_spherical_cap(raleigh, radius = 60000)
nc$share_near <- a5_count(a5_intersect(nc$cells, near_raleigh)) / a5_count(nc$cells)

state <- a5_union(nc$cells)
state
```

```{r recycle-plot, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 2.9}
share <- nc$share_near
steps <- ramp[c(2, 3, 5, 7)]
cols <- ifelse(share == 0, pal$base, steps[pmax(1, ceiling(share * 4))])
par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2))
plot(st_geometry(nc), col = cols, border = "white", lwd = 0.6)
lines(wk::wk_coords(circle(raleigh, 60000))[, c("x", "y")], col = pal$ink, lwd = 1.2)
legend("bottomleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.7, border = NA, text.col = pal$ink,
       fill = c(pal$base, steps),
       legend = c("none", "up to 25%", "25 to 50%", "50 to 75%", "75 to 100%"),
       title = "Share of county within 60 km of Raleigh", title.adj = 0)
```

Both coverings in each pair must be at the same resolution, or it is an
error. A5 cells do not nest across resolutions: a resolution-11 cell can
straddle the edge between two resolution-10 cells, so a set of cells at one
resolution does not translate into a set at another.

```{r mismatch, error = TRUE}
a5_union(state, a5_spherical_cap(a5_cell_to_parent(raleigh), radius = 60000))
```

```{r nest-plot, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 3.6, fig.height = 3, fig.align = "center"}
coarse_cells <- a5_uncompact(a5_grid_disk(a5_cell_to_parent(raleigh), k = 1))
fine_cells <- a5_cell_to_children(coarse_cells)
par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.2))
frame(cells_of(coarse_cells), main = "Resolution 11 cells over resolution 10 outlines")
fill(cells_of(fine_cells), pal$base, border = "white", lwd = 0.8)
outline(cells_of(coarse_cells), lwd = 1.4)
```

## Testing coverings

`a5_contains()` tests cells against a covering. Indexing points at the
covering's resolution turns it into a point-in-polygon test, decided cell by
cell: a point counts as inside when its cell belongs to the covering.

```{r contains}
set.seed(1)
lon <- stats::runif(300, -81.4, -80.9)
lat <- stats::runif(300, 36.35, 36.6)
points <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(lon, lat, resolution = 11)
inside <- a5_contains(centre, points)
table(inside)
```

```{r contains-plot, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 2.8}
par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.2))
frame(county, wk::xy(lon, lat), main = "a5_contains(centre, points)")
fill(cells_of(centre), pal$base)
outline(county)
points(lon[!inside], lat[!inside], pch = 21, bg = "white", col = pal$muted, cex = 0.7)
points(lon[inside], lat[inside], pch = 21, bg = pal$a, col = "white", cex = 0.9)
legend("bottomright", bty = "n", cex = 0.7, pch = 21, pt.cex = c(0.9, 0.7),
       pt.bg = c(pal$a, "white"), col = c("white", pal$muted), text.col = pal$ink,
       legend = c("TRUE", "FALSE"))
```

Near the county line the answer follows the cells, not the line: a point
just outside it is inside when its cell's centre is in the county, and the
reverse.

`a5_overlaps()` tests whether two coverings share any cell. With centre
containment every cell belongs to the one county holding its centre, so
neighbouring counties never overlap. With `containment = "overlapping"`,
cells along a shared border belong to both:

```{r overlaps}
pair <- nc[nc$NAME %in% c("Alleghany", "Ashe"), ]
by_centre <- a5_polygon_to_cells(pair, resolution = 11)
gap_free <- a5_polygon_to_cells(pair, resolution = 11, containment = "overlapping")
a5_overlaps(by_centre[1], by_centre[2])
a5_overlaps(gap_free[1], gap_free[2])
```

```{r overlaps-plot, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 2.4}
borders <- wk::as_wkb(st_geometry(pair))
panels(2)
for (step in list(list(by_centre, "centre: no shared cells"),
                  list(gap_free, "overlapping: shared border cells"))) {
  x <- step[[1]]
  frame(cells_of(gap_free), main = step[[2]])
  fill(cells_of(x[1]), paste0(pal$a, "b0"))
  fill(cells_of(x[2]), paste0(pal$b, "b0"))
  fill(cells_of(a5_intersect(x[1], x[2])), pal$result)
  outline(borders, lwd = 0.8)
}
```

Shared cells are in aqua.

## Drawing and joining

`a5_uncompact()` expands coverings to their cells. `simplify = FALSE` keeps
one element per covering, ready for `tidyr::unnest()`:

```{r uncompact}
per_county <- a5_uncompact(nc$cells[1:3], simplify = FALSE)
lengths(per_county)
```

Uncompacting can build a great many cells: a covering of France at
resolution 18 stands for about a billion. `a5_uncompact()` refuses to build
more than `.Machine$integer.max` cells; work with the covering itself where
possible.

## Storing coverings

Coverings keep their compaction marker in storage, as in the other A5
libraries. `a5_covering_to_arrow()` writes them to an Arrow `list<uint64>`
column that DuckDB, Python and JavaScript read with the resolution intact,
and `a5_covering_from_arrow()` reads them back, normalising coverings
written elsewhere. See `vignette("arrow-parquet")`. `a5_is_valid()` checks
that a covering built by hand is well formed.
